eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The study analyzes adult heart transplant recipients using random survival forests (a non‑linear machine learning model) to predict post‑transplant survival, meeting all population, intervention, outcome, and study design criteria.

identification_methods.Sponsorship source: NIH grants HL141892 and GM125072; Cystic Fibrosis Foundation
identification_methods.Setting: Retrospective analysis using the US Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients (SRTR)
identification_methods.Comments: Retrospective cohort study of adult heart transplant recipients analyzing survival phases with parametric temporal decomposition and random survival forests.
identification_methods.Institution: Cleveland Clinic, Heart and Vascular Institute
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Included all adult (≥18 years) isolated heart transplant recipients in SRTR from Jan 1, 2004 to Jul 1, 2018; excluded multi‑organ transplants and pediatric cases.
identification_methods.AI Model Architecture: Random Survival Forests (RSF) with 500 trees; also parametric temporal decomposition model
identification_methods.Input Variables: Recipient and donor demographics, clinical characteristics, laboratory values, mechanical circulatory support status, transplant era, insurance type, and other pre‑transplant variables.
identification_methods.Missing Data Handling: Multiple imputation by chained equations for parametric models; missForest imputation for random forest analysis.
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Temporal decomposition identified early, constant, and late hazard phases; RSF used to assess variable importance and interactions across time points (90 days, 1 yr, 5 yr, 10 yr).

population.Inclusion criteria: All adults in the SRTR who underwent isolated heart transplantation from January 1, 2004 to July 1, 2018
population.Exclusion criteria: Recipients of multi-organ transplants and recipients <18 years of age
population.Population Notes: Final cohort of 30,606 adult transplants after exclusions; median follow‑up 3.9 years

interventions_outcomes.Specific Algorithm Name: Random Survival Forests (RSF) and parametric non-proportional hazards temporal decomposition
interventions_outcomes.Intervention Input Data Modality: National registry data (Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients) with clinical variables
interventions_outcomes.Feature Selection Method: Machine‑learning variable selection within RSF and parsimonious modeling for sex interaction
interventions_outcomes.Temporal Handling: Temporal decomposition into early, constant, and late hazard phases; RSF evaluated at 90 days, 1 year, 5 years, and 10 years
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: Both conventional parametric time‑varying hazard modeling and non‑parametric RSF were applied to identify risk factors and interactions
interventions_outcomes.Reported outcomes in study: All‑cause mortality, survival rates at 90 days, 1 year, 5 years, and 10 years
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: Primary endpoint was time from transplant to death; survival curves generated for each temporal phase
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: Identified three mortality phases; sex was not a significant risk factor; numerous interactions affecting early, constant, and late mortality were discovered
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: Time from heart transplantation to death or end of follow‑up
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Timepoints: 90 days, 1 year, 5 years, 10 years (as evaluated by RSF)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: Sex not a significant predictor; risk factors varied by temporal phase
